notes: For several tools, exact response field names are produced by response helper methods (`includeSnapshot`, `setIncludePages`, `attachNetworkRequest`, etc.) whose implementations were not included. Where the source shows that the whole returned content can contain page/web data or identifiers but not precise field names, `return` is used for enforcement fields.

`evaluate_script`, `emulate`, and `take_heapsnapshot` behavior is partly based on the advertised command/source option definitions because their handlers were not included in the supplied source; these entries are marked `undetermined` where appropriate.

click.rationale: `click` performs a browser mouse click on a page element via `handle.asLocator().click(...)`. On an attacker-controlled page this is an observable browser interaction, so it is a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is true, the tool calls `response.includeSnapshot()`, returning page content that may be private and/or attacker-authored.

close_page.rationale: `close_page` closes a browser page selected by `pageId`, then includes the page list in the response. Open page titles/URLs can disclose the user's private browsing state and can also be attacker-authored by web pages.

drag.rationale: `drag` sends drag/drop input events to page elements (`fromHandle.drag`, `toHandle.drop`), which an attacker-controlled page can observe, so it is a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is true it returns a page snapshot, which can contain private or attacker-authored page content.

emulate.rationale: The advertised `emulate` arguments include `geolocation`, `userAgent`, and especially `extraHttpHeaders`, whose description says headers are included into every HTTP request from the page and persist across navigations. Those agent-supplied values can be delivered to web origins the page contacts. The implementation was not included, so reach beyond the advertised behavior is undetermined.

evaluate_script.rationale: The tool is advertised to execute an agent-supplied JavaScript function in the target page and may save output to `filePath`. The description example includes `fetch("example.com")`, so the script can contact attacker-chosen hosts from the browser page (SINK). Executed page JavaScript can return private page/account data, and on attacker-controlled pages can return attacker-authored content. Code for the handler was not included, so details of output formatting and limits are undetermined.

fill.rationale: `fill` writes the supplied `value` into a page element selected by `uid`, which can deliver agent-supplied text to an attacker-controlled page. If `includeSnapshot` is true, it returns a page snapshot that can contain private or attacker-authored content.

fill_form.rationale: `fill_form` iterates over supplied form `elements` and writes each nested value into the corresponding page element, delivering agent-supplied form data to the page. If `includeSnapshot` is true, it returns a page snapshot containing private and/or attacker-authored content.

get_console_message.rationale: `get_console_message` attaches a stored console message by `msgid`. Console messages come from the inspected page or extensions and can contain private page data or attacker-authored strings from attacker-controlled pages.

get_network_request.rationale: `get_network_request` returns or saves details for a selected network request. Its description explicitly says it is useful for inspecting request headers including `Cookie` and response headers including `Set-Cookie`, which are private account/browser data. Response bodies and headers from attacker-controlled hosts are attacker-authored. Optional file path parameters write request/response bodies to local files, making the tool WRITE, but the code does not show an attacker-readable destination.

handle_dialog.rationale: `handle_dialog` accepts or dismisses a browser dialog and may pass the agent-supplied `promptText` to `dialog.accept(...)`. A page that opened the prompt can read that text, so this is a SINK.

hover.rationale: `hover` sends mouse movement over a page element, which an attacker-controlled page can observe. If `includeSnapshot` is true, it returns page snapshot content that may be private or attacker-authored.

lighthouse_audit.rationale: `lighthouse_audit` audits the current page using Lighthouse, may perform navigation-mode reload, writes JSON/HTML reports, and returns a summary including the audited URL and report paths. Audit results and reports may include private page information; audited page content and URLs can be attacker-controlled.

list_console_messages.rationale: `list_console_messages` returns console data for the page via `response.setIncludeConsoleData(...)`. Console messages can disclose private page/account state and can be authored by attacker-controlled pages.

list_network_requests.rationale: `list_network_requests` includes recent network requests for the page. Request URLs and metadata can disclose private user/account activity, and URLs/metadata for attacker-controlled pages are attacker-authored. It returns identifiers usable by `get_network_request` through the request listing.

list_pages.rationale: `list_pages` returns the list of open browser pages via `response.setIncludePages(true)`. Page URLs/titles can reveal private browsing/account state, and page titles/URLs may be controlled by attacker-hosted pages.

navigate_page.rationale: `navigate_page` can navigate an existing page to an agent-supplied `url` using `page.pptrPage.goto(...)`, sending a browser request to that chosen destination. It can also install an agent-supplied `initScript` for the next navigation. The response includes page-list state, which can contain private or attacker-authored URLs/titles.

new_page.rationale: `new_page` creates a page and navigates it to the agent-supplied `url` with `page.pptrPage.goto(...)`, sending a browser request to an agent-chosen host. It then includes page-list state, whose titles/URLs can be private or attacker-authored.

performance_analyze_insight.rationale: `performance_analyze_insight` returns details from a previously recorded trace (`context.recordedTraces().at(-1)` and `response.attachTraceInsight(...)`). Trace insights can include private page URLs/timings and attacker-controlled page/resource URLs.

performance_start_trace.rationale: `performance_start_trace` records a browser trace, optionally reloads the page, may save raw trace data to `filePath`, parses the trace, stores it, and attaches a trace summary. Trace data and summaries can contain private page URLs/content/timings and attacker-controlled resource URLs/content. CrUX lookup is to a fixed Google endpoint, so it is not classified as a SINK under the stated rules.

performance_stop_trace.rationale: `performance_stop_trace` stops a running trace, may save raw trace data to `filePath`, parses the trace, stores it, and returns a summary. Trace data can include private page/account activity and attacker-controlled page/resource information.

press_key.rationale: `press_key` sends keyboard events to the page using the supplied `key`, which an attacker-controlled page can observe. If `includeSnapshot` is true, it returns a page snapshot containing private and/or attacker-authored content.

resize_page.rationale: `resize_page` changes the browser page/window size and then includes page-list state. Page-list URLs/titles can disclose private browsing state and can be attacker-authored by loaded pages.

select_page.rationale: `select_page` changes the selected page and may bring it to front, then includes page-list state. Page URLs/titles can reveal private browsing/account state and can be attacker-authored.

take_heapsnapshot.rationale: The advertised tool captures a heap snapshot of the target page and saves it to the supplied `filePath`. That can write private page memory to a local file, but the provided source does not show the snapshot content being returned into the agent context or sent to an attacker-readable destination. The handler implementation was not included, so output details are undetermined.

take_screenshot.rationale: `take_screenshot` captures an image of the page or element and either writes it to `filePath`/temporary file or attaches it to the response. Screenshots can reveal private page/account data, and screenshots of attacker-controlled pages are attacker-controllable visual content.

take_snapshot.rationale: `take_snapshot` returns or saves an accessibility-tree text snapshot of the target page. The snapshot contains page text and element identifiers, which can include private user/account content and attacker-authored page content.

type_text.rationale: `type_text` sends the agent-supplied `text` and optional `submitKey` into the currently focused page input via keyboard events. An attacker-controlled page can read the typed content, so this is a SINK.

upload_file.rationale: `upload_file` supplies local browser file paths to a page file input or file chooser (`handle.uploadFile` / `fileChooser.accept`), sending file contents to the page; an attacker-controlled page can receive those uploads, so it is a SINK. If `includeSnapshot` is true it returns a page snapshot, which can include private or attacker-authored content.

wait_for.rationale: `wait_for` waits until any supplied text appears, then always calls `response.includeSnapshot()`. The returned page snapshot can include private page/account content and attacker-authored page text.

value_conditions.default: off by default is false; JavaScript evaluation is enabled by default
value_conditions.effect: Disables JavaScript evaluation tools, removes `initScript` from `navigate_page`, and disallows `javascript:`, `data:`, and `vbscript:` navigations; this removes `evaluate_script` and part of the SINK surface of `navigate_page`.
Restricts browser network access by blocking URL patterns, reducing which hosts URL-navigation and page-initiated network SINKs can reach.
Restricts browser network access to allowed URL patterns only, reducing which hosts URL-navigation and page-initiated network SINKs can reach.
Disables sending URLs from performance traces to the fixed CrUX API endpoint for field data enrichment.
Limits filesystem paths accessible to file-writing and upload-related tool parameters to configured roots; default is the OS temp directory.
Disables the default path restriction when MCP roots are not negotiated, allowing file-writing tools and uploads to access paths outside the temp directory.

value_conditions.default: not set for normal MCP server
value_conditions.effect: When started by the CLI and no filesystem root is supplied, sets `allowUnrestrictedPaths=true` and removes the default filesystem root, making CLI file access broader than the MCP server default.
Exposes only a slim set of navigation, JavaScript execution, and screenshot tools, removing many advertised tools from the normal tool surface.
